# A logarithmic boundary cut excludes zero parameter faces at a bad minimum

This is a new auxiliary variational mechanism, not a proof of OC. The attainment theorem for the enlarged parameter class is being written independently by Slab. The present geometric argument is submitted for independent audit by Two-sided. Its quantitative estimates are stated explicitly below.

## 1. Setting and prerequisites

Fix a finite lattice-complete canonical base P, positive compatible d-dimensional fibers K_z, d>=1, and their canonical convex hull C. Let M=sum |K_z| and k be the number of occupied base parities. Set N=d+1. The underlying hypothetical bad compact family has positive lower fiber volumes, a common upper radius, and uniformly positive within-fiber covariance. Denote its covariance norm by G(u).

Allow nonnegative full-space concave functions L that are positive on the relative interior of every sampled fiber. Their logarithms are integrable on the mixed measure and are normalized by

    (1/M) integral_S log L = 0.

Use f(w)=(L(w)E_Kz(X)/M)^(1/N), with boundary value f=0, and the previous buffered cap depth with threshold N_cap.w-epsilon f(w)G(u). Assume the pair is an ACTUAL attained global minimum in this enlarged class, with raw maximum Q and beta=Q/M<1/k. The final OC-bad regime is stronger. There is no multiplier penalty.

Use the already proved strict proper stratum J, the atomic stratum A, uniqueness of a proper deepest mark per base, and the compressed old mass-Q atomic caps G_1,...,G_m covering A, where m<=k and beta m<1. If A is empty, no atomic cleanup is needed. Status heredity and the stronger disjoint-parity count are not needed for the numerical cut step beyond existence of such a cover.

All changes below are actual nested bodies and legal parameter normalizations. No physical differentiability of a mixed active-cap menu is assumed.

## 2. Finite supporting majorants at the actual proper marks

A full-space supporting plane at a boundary-base mark is not assumed. It can be constructed from the finite fiber family.

At a proper deepest mark w_p=(p,y_p), choose a finite continuous supergradient g of the concave function L(p,.) at its fiber-interior point y_p. Put

    phi_z=max_(X in K_z) [L(z,X)-g.X].

With the upper semicontinuous fiber representative this maximum exists. The array phi is sampled-concave: choose its maximizers in an anchored family, apply actual fiber inclusion and joint concavity, and then maximize at the target. Since phi_p=L(p,y_p)-g.y_p, a finite affine supporting majorant of the finite concave roof at p extends g to an affine A_p satisfying

    A_p>=L on every sampled fiber,  A_p(w_p)=L(w_p).

Each A_p is nonnegative on C=conv(S), and strictly positive on every sampled fiber interior. Define T=min_(p in J) A_p. It is concave and nonnegative on C; T>=L on S and equality holds at every proper deepest mark. An inequality between T and L at unsampled bases is unnecessary.

If T>L on a positive-volume set of S, use the concave raw path L+t(T-L) and normalize its logarithmic mean. The logarithmic normalization strictly decreases every old proper marked value. This remains true if the derivative integral is infinite: truncate the nonnegative ratio T/L-1 to obtain a fixed positive lower linear bound for the logarithmic normalization change. On sufficiently small fixed neighborhoods of the proper marks, continuity makes the relative raw increase smaller than that bound. Away from those neighborhoods the old depth has a strict compact gap, preserved by uniform convergence of the buffers. The old atomic caps still bound their entire fibers by Q. If the new maximum remains Q, every maximizing base is atomic and the actual all-atomic hinge theorem supplies a further arbitrarily small strict descent. This contradicts the global minimum.

Consequently T=L almost everywhere on S, and hence throughout each sampled fiber interior. Replacing L by T preserves the logarithmic normalization and every buffered depth: at fiber boundaries E=0. The new pair achieves the same global minimum. We may therefore take L itself to be the minimum of at most |J| affine nonnegative planes. This replacement does not assert equality of the original functions between integer fibers.

## 3. Exact logarithmic gain from an actual zero-face cut

Suppose this finite-plane L has a zero at some point v in a sampled fiber. One of its planes A has A(v)=0. It is nonnegative on C, positive at every sampled fiber-interior point, and L<=A on S.

For sufficiently small t>0, make the actual global cut

    C_t=C intersect {A>=t},   K_z(t)=K_z intersect {A(z,.)>=t}.

All fibers remain positive and compatible; taking their canonical hull does not change any sampled fiber. Let R_t be the removed mixed set and a_t its mass. Then a_t>0, a_t->0, and L<t on R_t. The exact new normalized parameter is L_t=c_t L, where

    log c_t=(integral_(R_t) log L)/(M-a_t)
             <=a_t log t/(M-a_t).                         (1)

Thus its logarithmic decrease is at least a_t |log t|/(M-a_t). Put h_t=a_t|log t|. Integrability of log L gives h_t->0, while h_t/a_t=|log t|->infinity. The cut therefore creates a normalization gain asymptotically larger than its volume cost.

For retained points, projective energy is monotone under inclusion:

    E_Kz(t)(X)<=E_Kz(X).

Every fiber's zeroth, first and second moments change by O(a_t), since the family is bounded and every old fiber has positive volume. The within-fiber covariance matrix therefore changes by O(a_t), and its positive definiteness gives G_t(u)<=[1+O(a_t)]G(u), uniformly over nonzero u. The total mass factor changes by 1+O(a_t). Equation (1) now yields, uniformly at every retained point,

    epsilon f_t(w)G_t(u)
        <=[1-c h_t] epsilon f(w)G(u)                    (2)

for some fixed c>0 and all sufficiently small t. This uses only an upper comparison; no derivative or two-sided energy estimate is required.

## 4. Uniform proper-cap improvement

Choose small fixed compact neighborhoods of all old proper deepest marks, inside their own fiber interiors. On them f has a positive lower bound, and each base has the fixed gap b_base(p)-Q>0.

Normalize a continuous cap normal by |u|=1. A cap of old mass at most Q+o(1) based at such a point cannot have its own threshold arbitrarily close to the lower support of K_p. If the distance were s, lowering the whole ambient threshold by s would contain K_p. The whole-own-fiber capture lemma gives resulting mass at least b_base(p); the total added mass is at most C s by the uniform upper section-area bound, independently of the integer tilt. The base gap therefore gives a fixed positive lower-support distance. The upper-support distance is also uniformly positive, since the threshold lies below the source by its positive buffer and the source stays in an interior core.

Sections of a fixed positive convex fiber at thresholds staying uniformly between its two support levels have a uniform positive (d-1)-volume lower bound over unit u. This follows by compactness and interior section continuity, or directly by the common inner-cone bound; d=1 uses section measure one. Thus increasing any such threshold by a small s removes at least c_0 s of OWN volume.

Apply this to caps approaching the old infimum, with approximation error o(h_t). The own-strip loss from (2) is at least c_1 h_t, whereas the actual body cut can only remove additional cap mass. Taking the infimum gives

    b_t(w)<=b(w)-c_1 h_t<=Q-c_1 h_t                 (3)

uniformly on the retained proper neighborhoods. Approximate minimizers suffice; arbitrary supporting incidences at the other fibers cause no problem. The entire old proper maximizing set lies in these neighborhoods. Outside them, at proper bases and at all old nondeepest bases, a fixed old gap remains, since (2) and nesting give b_t(w)<=b(w). Division by M-a_t costs only O(a_t), so the proper normalized maxima fall by order h_t.

At old atomic bases the unchanged fixed base caps merely give b_t<=Q. Their normalized upper bound is beta+O(a_t); this possible increase is not discarded.

## 5. Quantitative atomic cleanup costs only order a_t

Retain the old m compressed atomic caps, each of old mass Q. Choose nonnegative convex base hinges supported exactly on their sampled traces. At the CUT family, divide each hinge by its actual surface-area cost, and sum them. The resulting actual compatible inner erosion of duration s has total first mass loss m and first loss at least one in each selected cap.

These expansions are uniform as t->0 and s->0: the cut fibers converge in Hausdorff distance to fixed positive fibers; their inner parallel bodies also do, and surface area is continuous on this compact positive family. Equivalently integrate the inner parallel surface areas over the duration. The normalized selected-cap upper derivative is at most

    -[1-(beta+O(a_t))m]/(M-a_t),

bounded above by a fixed negative number. Choose s_t=C a_t with fixed C sufficiently large. Every selected cap, and therefore every mark at every old atomic base, then has normalized mass strictly below the ORIGINAL beta, by order a_t.

It remains to retain the proper improvement. Let D be the mass removed by this second nested erosion. Its logarithmic renormalization relative to the already normalized L_t has the exact scalar exponent

    (integral_removed log L_t)/(M_t-D).

Since log L_t is bounded ABOVE uniformly, this exponent is at most O(D)=O(s_t), even if other zero faces remain. Negative logarithmic values help. Energy decreases under the erosion; covariance and mass change by O(s_t). Hence physical buffers grow by at most a factor 1+O(s_t). The all-normal upper slab bound gives a uniform depth increase at most O(s_t). This estimate retains every supporting cap status and every integer tilt.

The loss c_1 h_t in (3) dominates O(s_t)=O(a_t). Thus all proper bases stay strictly below the original normalized beta; all old nondeepest bases retain their fixed gap. Every possible new maximum has been covered. The final actual compatible pair has normalized maximum strictly less than beta, contradicting global minimality.

If the atomic set was empty, the first cut already supplies this contradiction and Section 5 is unnecessary.

## 6. Conclusion and what it does not prove

Subject to the separately established enlarged-class attainment and the audited prior atomic/energy inputs, an attained bad minimum has an equivalent finite-plane parameter L that is STRICTLY POSITIVE on every sampled fiber, and therefore on C. The logarithmic boundary singularity has been excluded by an actual body variation, not an assumed compactness of positive affine parameters.

This restores both signs of affine parameter perturbations and permits the full-space analogue of the nonregular volume transport. It does not identify those parameter weights with a physical surface separator, prove an ordinary Gamma payment, or exhaust original mixed mass by a parity budget. Full OC remains unproved.
